key_insight: FrontierPhysics moves AI evaluation beyond isolated physics questions toward end-to-end research. Its 56 expert-created tasks aim to assess research quality alongside correctness.
problem_solved: Existing physics benchmarks focus on fixed questions, isolated subtasks, or reproducing papers with known solutions, leaving agents’ ability to conduct complete, high-quality research under-tested.
method: Build 56 research tasks contributed by 42 physicists based on their own work.
Cover nine domains spanning theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Evaluate end-to-end research with attention to both correctness and research quality; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify the full workflow or scoring.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, FrontierPhysics offers a more research-oriented framework for evaluating scientific agents. It shifts attention from solving predefined problems to producing scientifically valuable work.
visual_elements: Three headline counters: 56 tasks, 42 physicists, nine domains.
A comparison diagram contrasting isolated-question benchmarks with end-to-end research evaluation.
Three connected icons representing theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
A two-axis evaluation graphic highlighting correctness and research quality.
paper_title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
paper_authors: Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer, Bo Liu, Wenbo Chen
